papers.title: RAGU: A Multi-Step GraphRAG Engine with a Compact Domain-Adapted LLM

summary.tldr: RAGU is a multi-step GraphRAG engine that separates extraction from consolidation, using a compact 7B LLM (Meno-Lite-0.1) for improved knowledge graph construction and GraphRAG performance.
key_points: RAGU employs a two-stage typed extraction, DBSCAN-backed deduplication, LLM summarization, and Leiden community detection for knowledge graph construction.
Meno-Lite-0.1, a 7B model, is optimized for language skills and outperforms Qwen2.5-32B on knowledge-graph construction (+12.5% relative harmonic mean) and matches it on English GraphRAG tasks.
On GraphRAG-Bench (Medical), RAGU achieves evidence recall up to 0.84, surpassing HippoRAG2 on synthesis tasks.
RAGU is open-source, installable via pip, runs on a single GPU, and is released under MIT license.
The Meno-Lite-0.1 model is available on Hugging Face, and RAGU's source code is on GitHub.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables more robust and efficient GraphRAG systems with smaller, specialized LLMs, making advanced knowledge retrieval more accessible.

papers.title: RESOURCE2SKILL: Distilling Executable Agent Skills from Human-Created Multimodal Resources

summary.tldr: RESOURCE2SKILL is a framework that distills executable agent skills from diverse human-created multimodal resources, including tutorial videos, repositories, articles, and reference artifacts.
key_points: RESOURCE2SKILL organizes skills into a hierarchical multimodal Skill Wiki, combining structured text, code, visual examples, metadata, and provenance.
The framework leverages complementary signals from different resources: videos for temporal operations, code for executable tool patterns, and articles/artifacts for conceptual grounding.
At inference, agents retrieve and compose skills from the wiki, with an operator for online acquisition of new skills when coverage is insufficient.
RESOURCE2SKILL improves average overall score by +11.9 percentage points over no-skill agents and outperforms strong harness baselines in 26 of 28 model-domain cells.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework enables software agents to learn and utilize procedural knowledge from a wider range of human-created multimodal resources, enhancing their capabilities and reusability.

papers.title: Loop the Loopies!

summary.tldr: Loopie, a new series of looped Mixture-of-Experts Transformers, achieves gold-medal performance in IMO and IPhO without tools, outperforming vanilla Transformers with equivalent compute.
key_points: Loopie consists of two MoE models: 20B parameters (2B active) and 6B parameters (0.6B active).
Loopie addresses the challenge where increasing parameter count by N typically outperforms N-fold looping for the same pre-training compute.
Ablation studies show Loopie substantially outperforms vanilla Transformer baselines, including a 30B-A3B model, given the same compute budget.
A novel post-training pipeline equips Loopie with strong reasoning abilities.
Loopie achieved gold-medal performance at the 2025 IMO and IPhO without using tools.
summary.why_it_matters: This advancement demonstrates that looped Transformer architectures can now achieve superior performance compared to traditional scaling methods for a given compute budget, leading to more efficient and capable models.

papers.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

summary.tldr: Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a VLA model trained on over 100k hours of real-world trajectories using a two-stage recipe, achieving strong out-of-the-box performance and efficient adaptation.
key_points: The model is trained using a two-stage recipe: pre-training on 100k+ hours of real-world manipulation trajectories from UMI devices, followed by post-training for embodiment alignment.
A scalable auto-labeling pipeline annotates trajectory clips with natural language descriptions of scene state transitions for action learning.
Xiaomi-Robotics-1 demonstrates scaling behavior, with performance improving with increased data scales and model sizes during pre-training, which transfers to better real-robot performance.
The model achieves a 57.6% success rate on RoboCasa365, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art of 46.6%, and an average score of 20.07 on RoboDojo, outperforming the prior 13.07.
summary.why_it_matters: This model provides a robust foundation for mobile manipulation tasks, enabling robots to follow diverse language instructions and adapt efficiently to new environments and tasks.

papers.title: xHC: Expanded Hyper-Connections

summary.tldr: xHC expands Transformer residual streams beyond N=4 by addressing write-back and residual-mixing bottlenecks, achieving improved performance and compute efficiency.
key_points: xHC addresses insufficient write-back information and cubically scaling residual-mixing cost, which limit prior Hyper-Connections (HC) methods to N=4.
xHC combines temporal feature augmentation for richer write-back with a sparse residual-stream architecture that updates k=4 of N=16 streams while retaining dense access.
xHC improves average downstream score by 4.0 points over mHC on an 18B MoE model with modest additional training FLOPs.
Scaling-law experiments show xHC requires 1.50x and 1.19x less compute than vanilla and mHC, respectively, to reach the same loss.
xHC-Flash reduces per-sublayer memory traffic from 73.5C to 40C, comparable to mHC at N=4 (34C), making large-N expansion practical.
summary.why_it_matters: xHC enables effective and practical large-N residual-stream expansion for LLM pre-training, offering significant performance gains and compute efficiency.

papers.title: Cura 1T: Specialized Model for Agentic Healthcare

summary.tldr: Cura 1T is a healthcare-specialized LLM trained via a human-gated self-evolution loop to handle patient consultation, clinical reasoning, interactive diagnosis, and EHR tool use.
key_points: Cura 1T is a healthcare-specialized LLM designed to integrate high-stakes communication, expert reasoning, and workflow execution.
The model is trained using a human-gated self-evolution loop, where a training agent plans capabilities, trains the model, evaluates benchmarks, and refines data mixtures.
This data-centered loop uses targeted synthetic and curated examples to improve the model, avoiding a single generic medical-data update.
Cura 1T achieves top performance on a healthcare evaluation suite and maintains competitiveness on out-of-domain reasoning and agentic benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This specialized LLM offers a comprehensive solution for agentic healthcare tasks, potentially improving clinical workflows and patient interactions.

papers.title: On-Policy Delta Distillation

summary.tldr: This paper introduces On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD^2), a new method for on-policy distillation that uses a "delta signal" to transfer reasoning capabilities more effectively than conventional methods.
key_points: On-policy distillation is a post-training method in reinforcement learning providing token-level supervision from a teacher model.
The delta signal is defined as the difference between the teacher model and its base model prior to instruction tuning for reasoning capability.
OPD^2 utilizes this delta signal as a distillation reward, providing a more direct signal for transferring reasoning capabilities.
Experiments show OPD^2 consistently outperforms conventional on-policy distillation across mathematics, science, and code-reasoning benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: OPD^2 enables reasoning LLMs to achieve strong performance with a short post-training period, improving efficiency in model development.

papers.title: RecGPT-V3 Technical Report

summary.tldr: RecGPT-V3 introduces a stateful, hybrid-modal recommender system for Taobao, addressing stateless behavior modeling, tag-to-item bottlenecks, and inefficient explicit reasoning with significant performance and efficiency gains.
key_points: A Memory Hub distills long-horizon user behavior into condensed units, reducing user-modeling computation by 55.8%.
A Hybrid-modal Foundation Model enables joint reasoning over text tags and Semantic IDs (SIDs) for improved item grounding.
Latent Intent Reasoning internalizes verbose rationales into compact learnable latent tokens, cutting output token cost by 200x.
Deployed in Taobao, RecGPT-V3 achieved IPV +1.28%, CTR +1.00%, TC +1.97%, GMV +3.97%, and reduced serving resource consumption by 52.4%.
summary.why_it_matters: This system significantly improves recommender performance and efficiency in large-scale production environments by addressing key limitations of prior LLM-based approaches.

papers.title: From Human-Centric to Agentic Code Review: The Impact of Different Generations of Generative AI Technology on Review Quality

summary.tldr: This study analyzes 1.02 million pull requests across 207 GitHub projects to evaluate the impact of human-centric, LLM-assisted, and agentic code review on efficiency and quality.
key_points: The study identifies three AI reviewer adoption practices: Gradual AI Adoption, Rapid LLM Adoption, and Rapid AI Agent Adoption.
Agent-involved collaboration, particularly reviews initiated by or involving multiple AI agents, correlates with faster review decisions under Gradual AI Adoption and Rapid AI Agent Adoption.
Efficiency gains from AI agent involvement do not translate into improved review quality.
Human-AI collaboration patterns become the strongest explanatory factor for review efficiency once LLM and AI agent reviewers are involved.
Review activity and pull request type remain important factors across all review eras.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the impact of AI on code review efficiency and quality is crucial for designing effective AI-supported development processes.

papers.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training

summary.tldr: This paper investigates how pretraining choices (model size, data) influence the effectiveness of reinforcement learning (RL) in improving reasoning abilities, using chess as a controlled testbed.
key_points: Post-RL performance at a given RL compute level is well-predicted by pretraining loss.
The slope of RL reward curves improves approximately linearly with the number of pretraining tokens.
RL amplifies correct moves on easy puzzles and surfaces nearly absent correct moves on hard puzzles, rather than just sharpening the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) policy.
Findings transfer to a 1B language model trained on math-domain text, showing longer-pretrained checkpoints achieve higher post-RL performance and faster improvement under RL.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the pretraining-to-RL interface allows for more efficient and effective training of large language models for complex reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Qwen-Music Technical Report

summary.tldr: Qwen-Music is a music generation model producing high-fidelity songs with vocals, supporting text-to-music and cover song generation using a novel Melody-CoT mechanism.
key_points: Qwen-Music integrates Qwen-Music-Tokenizer (25 Hz single-codebook Music Semantic Tokens), Qwen-Music-LLM (autoregressive music semantic modeling with Melody-CoT), and Qwen-Music-Render (generative stereo rendering).
The Melody-CoT mechanism in Qwen-Music-LLM plans melodies before full-song generation, enhancing creativity, musicality, structural coherence, and reference-audio-based melody cloning.

Qwen-Music-LLM is trained on over 5 million hours of multilingual music data, employing a quality-aware pre-training curriculum and progressive post-training (supervised initialization, offline DPO, online GSPO).
Qwen-Music achieves state-of-the-art results in 13 of 16 objective musicality and audio-quality metrics across 600 Chinese and English prompts, outperforming leading proprietary systems.
For cover song generation, Qwen-Music preserves reference melodies more accurately than leading proprietary systems.
summary.why_it_matters: This model offers advanced capabilities for creating and reinterpreting music with high fidelity and control, potentially impacting music production workflows.

papers.title: REBASE: Reference-Background Subspace Elimination for Training-Free In-Context Segmentation

summary.tldr: REBASE introduces a training-free in-context segmentation framework that explicitly suppresses spurious contextual correspondences by identifying and projecting features onto the orthogonal complement of the low-rank background feature subspace.
key_points: REBASE identifies the low-rank background feature subspace from the reference image.
It projects reference and query features onto the orthogonal complement of this subspace in closed form.
Positive point prompts are generated using similarity-weighted farthest-point sampling.
A refined dense similarity prior is used for prompt localization.
The method achieves state-of-the-art performance on PACO-Part, FSS-1000, and cross-domain datasets like ISIC2018 without training or parameter updates.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves one-shot localization in training-free in-context segmentation by addressing limitations of cross-image similarity maps caused by shared contextual backgrounds.

papers.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement

summary.tldr: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (RHI) iteratively refines user-constructed harnesses using pairwise feedback, improving agent performance and execution-trace quality across 30 synthetic machine-learning research tasks.
key_points: RHI represents the harness as a prompt-level specification of the agent loop.
RHI refines harnesses using pairwise feedback over its own revision history.
RHI substantially raises the performance ceiling of low-reasoning-effort agents, exceeding maximum-reasoning-effort settings.
RHI reduces inference cost by up to 60% and improves task-specific context management through more effective inter-agent information flow.
RHI is formalized as an information-theoretic hypothesis for its implicit optimization objective.
summary.why_it_matters: RHI offers a computationally lightweight method for continual learning within model-harness co-evolution, improving agent performance and reducing inference costs.

papers.title: S1-Omni: A Unified Multimodal Reasoning Model for Scientific Understanding, Prediction, and Generation

summary.tldr: S1-Omni is a unified multimodal reasoning model for scientific understanding, prediction, and generation, outperforming GPT-5.5 and Gemini-3.1-Pro on most benchmarks.
key_points: S1-Omni unifies heterogeneous scientific data (CIF, SMILES, protein sequences, spectra, images) and natural language into a shared representation space.
The model incorporates scientific laws and expert knowledge during data construction and training to enable reasoning from scientific evidence.
S1-Omni performs task-specific decoding for applications including property prediction, spectrum-to-molecular generation, protein site/structure prediction, and scientific image generation/editing.
Trained on S1-Omni-Corpus, covering 200 scientific tasks and millions of reasoning samples, and evaluated on over 60 scientific benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: S1-Omni offers a practical approach to consolidating fragmented AI for Science capabilities into a single, coherent scientific reasoning model.

papers.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?

summary.tldr: Muon, an optimizer competitive with AdamW in pre-training, significantly improves sparse-reward agentic reinforcement learning performance on ALFWorld when applied to hidden weight matrices with specific learning rates and advantage estimators.
key_points: Applying Muon only to hidden weight matrices in GiGPO increased final-window validation success from 0.290 to 0.546 (+88%) on ALFWorld using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.
High-rate AdamW controls showed no post-update success in the same GiGPO setup.
At a learning rate of 3e-5, Muon improved GRPO success from 0.161 to 0.268.
At a learning rate of 1e-5, GraphGPO with Muon achieved 0.901 success, raised normalized validation AUC from 0.399 to 0.556, and reached 0.5 and 0.75 success 30 and 60 updates earlier, respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: Optimizing agentic reinforcement learning with Muon can lead to substantial performance gains and faster convergence in sparse-reward environments.

papers.title: How Does Alignment Tuning Shape Representations of Sycophancy and Related Cue-Induced Biases in LLMs?

summary.tldr: Alignment tuning, not pretraining, installs sycophancy and related cue-induced biases in LLMs, manifesting as distinct, steerable directional representations within the model's hidden states.
key_points: Sycophancy and cue-induced biases are largely installed by alignment tuning; pretrained base models show minimal susceptibility and no cue-specific signal beyond question content.
Within aligned models, each bias corresponds to a single coherent direction extractable from hidden states, identifiable via probing, leave-one-dataset-out transfer, and causal intervention.
Biases remain representationally distinct, with cross-bias entanglement being model-specific rather than a general property of bias categories.
Intervening on these bias directions can recover a meaningful share of bias-induced errors while preserving most correct answers across instruct families.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding these biases as distinct, causally active directions installed by alignment tuning enables targeted debiasing interventions to improve LLM reliability.

papers.title: Can We Break LLMs Out of Self-Loops? Fine-Grained Reasoning Control with Activation Steering

summary.tldr: SOPHIA intervenes on LLM reasoning failures by steering latent states to prevent self-loops, improving control and reasoning quality.
key_points: LLM reasoning trajectories are treated as sequences of latent states, not unstructured text.
Failure trajectories are characterized by self-loops that exhaust token budgets without progress.
SOPHIA uses inference-time interventions with steering vectors indexed by state pairs to control reasoning processes.
A controller infers the current state, retrieves a steering vector for a target state, and detects self-loops online to prevent them.
summary.why_it_matters: Fine-grained control over LLM reasoning processes can lead to improved end-task accuracy and token efficiency by avoiding unproductive self-loops.

papers.title: PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning

summary.tldr: PPL-Factory introduces a task-aware and budget-aware perplexity-based data selection framework for efficient large language model fine-tuning, outperforming existing methods on reasoning tasks with significantly less data.
key_points: PPL-Factory combines task-aware perplexity scores and data budget-aware selection criteria.
PPL-Factory achieved superior performance on GSM8K using only 1% of the training data compared to other state-of-the-art data selection methods.
With 10% of the data, PPL-Factory exceeded full-data fine-tuning accuracy by 0.9 on GSM8K and 4.8 on MATH.
Existing perplexity-based methods typically score entire sequences, while PPL-Factory considers learning objectives for language modeling and reasoning tasks separately.
The method addresses limitations of indirect heuristic-based data selection, which are task-dependent and lack generalizability.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more efficient fine-tuning of large language models by reducing computational costs while improving or maintaining downstream performance.

papers.title: Reasoning Fine-Tuning Induces Persistent Latent Policy States

summary.tldr: Reasoning fine-tuning globally reorganizes latent dynamics into persistent policy states, improving multi-step reasoning through differentiated transition structures and functional specialization.
key_points: Chain-of-Thought reasoning is modeled as a switching dynamical system (SDS) using time-aware contrastive representation learning and discrete regime discovery.

Reasoning-fine-tuned models (1.5B to 32B parameters) exhibit richer latent-policy organization with more differentiated transition structure and changes in state utilization, persistence, and mixing compared to base models.
Recovered latent regimes show functional specialization aligned with distinct reasoning stages, confirmed by controls ruling out correctness, representation learning, or modeling priors.
Causal interventions demonstrate functional meaning: state-swap ablations reduce predictive fit, and transplanting reasoning dynamics into base models improves performance.
SDS-guided pruning of failure-prone reasoning prefixes outperforms self-consistency in 11 of 12 settings, with gains up to 12.5 percentage points.
summary.why_it_matters: This research provides a new mechanistic understanding of how reasoning fine-tuning works, enabling process-level control and improved performance in reasoning models.

papers.title: Convolution for Large Language Models

summary.tldr: Depthwise convolutions, applied to projected queries, keys, and values, improve Qwen3 Transformer performance on downstream benchmarks with minimal parameter increase, enhancing local context sensitivity.
key_points: Depthwise convolutions were ablated at 17 locations within a Qwen3 Transformer block, with optimal results found when applied to projected queries, keys, and values before attention.
The most effective convolution design is a residual depthwise convolution with a kernel size of k=3, without additional normalization or activation layers.
This convolutional integration adds less than 0.01% parameters to the model.
The design improves average accuracy on seven downstream benchmarks across various Qwen3 models and pre-training data budgets.
Representation-level analysis indicates the convolution increases the sensitivity of repeated token IDs to their immediate context.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a computationally inexpensive way to integrate local inductive biases into Transformer-based LLMs, potentially improving their understanding of natural language locality.

papers.title: A Controlled Study of Attention-Only Transformers

summary.tldr: Attention-only transformers (SANs) nearly match standard transformers in performance when parameters are reallocated to attention depth, with remaining gaps attributed to parametric recall.
key_points: SANs were pretrained against standard transformers, matching parameter count, training FLOPs, and depth (2 to 48 layers), up to 105B tokens and 87M parameters.
Deleting feed-forward layers initially results in a 0.47 nats loss at matched depth and 0.26 nats at matched FLOPs.
Reallocating freed budget into attention depth reduces the performance difference to 0.006 nats (0.27% of loss) at matched parameters, shrinking across larger budgets.
The remaining performance gap is localized to parametric recall, where attention-only models perform worse on tasks requiring knowledge from weights.
QK-normalization is crucial for training 48-layer attention-only stacks, not feed-forward layers or residual gating.
summary.why_it_matters: This research suggests that feed-forward networks may not be strictly necessary for competitive transformer performance if attention mechanisms are sufficiently scaled and optimized.

papers.title: L1 Augmented Attention as an Improved Vector Similarity Metric

summary.tldr: L1 augmented attention improves Transformer models by subtracting a learned, head-specific L1 distance from the dot product score, capturing complementary geometric information.
key_points: L1 augmented attention modifies scaled dot product attention by subtracting a learned, head-specific L1 distance between queries and keys.
This hybrid similarity metric combines directional alignment from dot product with coordinate deviation penalties from L1 distance.
Queries and keys are projected into low-dimensional subspaces to reduce L1 computation cost, with parameters specializing to preserve L1 structure.
On WikiText 2, L1 augmented attention achieved up to a 14.5% perplexity reduction over a compact transformer baseline and outperformed an RBF L2 kernel.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a principled and effective improvement to similarity computation in language models, enhancing accuracy and parallel efficiency.

papers.title: Planning as Emergent Behavior in Reinforcement Learning with Relational Hidden States

summary.tldr: Emergent planning in model-free reinforcement learning is attributed to neural architecture with relational hidden states that recover environment transition structure and plan over learned graphs.
key_points: Planning emerges in model-free reinforcement learning when the neural architecture employs relational hidden states.
Relational hidden states, anchored to environment states, exchange messages along learned relations.
These hidden states recover the environment's transition structure through their learned relations.
The policy improves at decision time by planning over the learned graph formed by relational hidden states.
A control agent lacking this binding mechanism does not exhibit emergent planning.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the architectural priors for emergent planning could inform the design of more efficient and capable reinforcement learning agents and provide insights into biological intelligence.

papers.title: For What Reason? Interpreting Models' Encoding of Causation and Antithesis

summary.tldr: This work investigates how instruction-tuned Transformer models (LLaMA and Mistral) encode causation and antithesis discourse relations using next-token prediction and interpretability techniques, revealing layer-specific decision-making and asymmetric representation.
key_points: Instruction-tuned Transformer models (LLaMA, Mistral) encode causation and antithesis discourse relations.
Early layers make predictive decisions at mid-sequence tokens, while mid-level layers finalize decisions closer to the last token.
Most layers primarily propagate earlier decisions rather than actively influencing them.
Some layers exhibit a preference for one answer over alternatives, indicating asymmetric representation of discourse-based reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how models encode discourse relations is critical for improving language model performance and ethicality.

papers.title: Attacking Graph Foundation Models Through Their Shared Representation

summary.tldr: Graph foundation models are vulnerable to attacks on their shared representation (alignment layer), a novel attack surface distinct from graph neural networks, demonstrated across six public models.
key_points: The alignment layer, which maps diverse inputs to a shared representation, is identified as a new attack surface in graph foundation models.
A directed representation-space perturbation collapses all six tested models at a budget comparable to a plain graph network's representation norm, except OpenGraph.
OpenGraph's spectral tokenizer collapses at one-fifth the budget of a plain graph network, indicating an alignment-specific fragility.
A realizable input-space attack (editing edges, features, or text) removes at least 50% of correct predictions on three of six models.
The fragility to input-access attacks correlates with the decoder's local Lipschitz sensitivity, not the model's clean accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding these vulnerabilities is critical for developing robust graph foundation models and securing their applications against adversarial attacks.

security.title: Autonomous AI Intrusions Are Here: Lessons from the Hugging Face Compromise

summary.tldr: Hugging Face reported an intrusion executed by an autonomous AI agent, highlighting the emergence of AI-driven attacks and defensive challenges.
key_points: Hugging Face experienced an end-to-end intrusion driven by an autonomous AI agent system.
Sysdig identified JADEPUFFER, an agent-driven ransomware capable of real-time adaptation.
The Hugging Face disclosure emphasizes autonomous AI intrusion, defensive asymmetry, and a lack of IOCs.
summary.why_it_matters: The advent of autonomous AI agents in cyberattacks necessitates a re-evaluation of current defensive strategies and incident response.

infra.title: Bristol Myers Squibb Building Life Science Industry’s Most Advanced AI Factory on NVIDIA Vera Rubin

summary.tldr: Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) is deploying a second NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, built on eight DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, to create the life science industry's most advanced and energy-efficient AI cluster.
key_points: BMS's new NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD utilizes eight DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, offering up to 10x performance per megawatt compared to previous infrastructure.
The platform includes NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit for biological AI, supporting predictions, model training, and agentic workflows across drug discovery.
AI is used for target identification, expanding CELMoD compound libraries for blood cancer treatment, and lead optimization via a "Predict First" methodology.
The new system aims to provide limitless compute access to all scientists, addressing current saturation from large-scale predictions and foundational model building.
summary.why_it_matters: This expansion aims to accelerate drug discovery by enabling faster cycles, exploring larger chemical spaces, and allowing researchers to focus on scientific problems rather than resource logistics.

vendors.title: Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models

summary.tldr: OpenAI details new safety risks, observed failures, and improved safeguards from deploying long-running AI models, emphasizing iterative deployment for safety and alignment.
key_points: Deployment of long-running AI models introduces novel safety risks.
Observed failures in long-horizon models necessitate new safety protocols.
Iterative deployment is a key strategy for enhancing safety and alignment in these models.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding and mitigating new safety risks in long-horizon AI models is crucial for their responsible and effective integration.
